column6: Early block dropout preserves 140.1 passes but loses 0.55 points and worsens test loss, showing additive regularization harms this WRN.

column6: Removing late weight decay preserves exposure but loses 0.33 points and sharply worsens test loss, so continuous decay remains beneficial.

column5: Decoupled cosine-to-zero floor with preserved warmup
column6: Annealing the hard-label tail to zero preserves exposure but loses 0.27 points, so the accepted 0.002 floor supports useful late refinement.

column5: BF16 autocast training with FP32 master weights
column6: BF16 delivered 12.1% more exposure and halved VRAM but lost 0.26 points with worse loss, so this faster numerical path does not help.

column5: Selective 160-channel final WRN stage
column6: Selective low-resolution width gained 0.04 points at 132.2 passes but missed the margin, showing capacity is promising yet this allocation is insufficient.

column5: One extra 128-channel residual block in the 8x8 stage
column6: An extra 8x8 residual block gains 0.08 points at 132.9 passes but misses the margin; exact [2,2,3] depth is insufficient.

column5: Exact rank-64 post-stage-3 bottleneck residual refinement
column6: The efficient bottleneck retained 135.5 passes but lost 0.33 points; constrained low-rank refinement does not preserve the prior capacity gain.

column5: Late whole-state EMA from the hard-label transition
column6: Whole-state EMA retained 141.0 passes and gained 0.03 points, but lagged terminal refinement and missed the 94.17 margin.

column5: Zero-initialize all six residual endpoint convolutions
column6: Identity-biased residual initialization preserved 142.8 passes but lost 0.19 points; the accepted Kaiming residual startup is better calibrated.

column5: Independent per-example alpha-0.2 mixup coefficients through the accepted 65% window
column6: Per-example coefficient diversity preserved exposure but lost 0.28 points, indicating batch-shared mixup strength variation is beneficial in this WRN.

column5: Fixed-MAC WRN stage-depth redistribution from [2,2,2] to [1,2,3]
column6: Moving one early block late delivered 171.7 passes but lost 0.25 points, showing high-resolution refinement is essential despite slower kernels.

column5: Exact-identity ratio-16 squeeze-and-excitation on both stage-3 residual branches
column6: Feature-driven stage-3 gates improved loss and added 0.09 points, but their 4.6% overhead left the run 0.01 below acceptance.

column5: Exact-neutral ratio-16 squeeze-and-excitation on the final stage-3 residual branch only
column6: Final-only SE recovered exposure but lost 0.40 points; the first gate attenuation or two-gate interaction drove EXP017 near-positive result.

column5: Learned static first-stage-3 channel scale plus final-block ratio-16 SE
column6: Static scales learned the expected 0.675 attenuation but scored 93.86, showing input dependence or two-gate co-adaptation matters.

column5: Extend batch-shared alpha-0.2 mixup cutoff from 65% to 75%
column6: A 75% cutoff preserved 141.59 passes but lost 0.25 points, placing the mixup-duration optimum near the accepted 65% window.

column5: Rho-0.05 SAM during the final 10% counted-time window
column6: Final-window SAM steps cost 2.15x normal and projected only 89.67% whole-run retention, failing the preregistered feasibility floor before scoring.

column5: Alternating rho-0.05 SAM during the final 10% counted-time window
column6: Alternating late SAM retained 136.99 passes but lost 0.28 points, so feasible sparse sharpness updates still disrupt terminal top-1 refinement.

column5: Selective 160-channel stage 3 with full two-gate squeeze-and-excitation
column6: The diagnostic-free width-plus-SE composition projected 126.21 passes, missing its fixed 127-pass feasibility floor before scoring.

column5: Two exact-neutral diagonal conditional stage-3 residual gates
column6: Diagonal self-gating retained 138.96 passes but scored 93.91, indicating both placement and input dependence are insufficient without cross-channel interaction.

column5: Diagnostic-free full two-gate squeeze-and-excitation closure
column6: Removing gate diagnostics still projected only 136.90 passes, narrowly missing the preregistered 137-pass feasibility floor before scoring.

column5: Worker-safe early-only one-operation RandAugment
column6: Early mild RandAugment preserved exact clean-tail RNG and 142.45 passes, gaining 0.05 points but missing the required 94.17% margin.

column5: Extra final WRN block plus worker-safe early RandAugment
column6: Early image invariance unlocks extra low-resolution capacity, turning two standalone near-misses into a 0.25-point fixed-budget improvement.

column5: Freeze stem and stage 1 after the 65% exhausted boundary
column6: Freezing 3.4% high-resolution parameters cut hard-tail step time 35.9% but lost 0.33 points, proving their late adaptation remains essential.

column5: Batch 128 with fully scaled 0.1-to-0.001 LR curve
column6: Batch 128 retained under 90.22% of accepted image throughput, missing fixed 120-pass and 46,875-update feasibility floors before scoring.

column5: Early p=0.05 private-RNG drop-path on the added stage-3 block
column6: Even narrow early masking of the added block regressed accuracy and loss at normal exposure; preserve its full residual contribution.

column6: Channels-last preserved logical state but exceeded fixed NCHW/NHWC logit tolerances before timing; close exact layout conversion without scoring.

column5: Three-point terminal parameter average
column6: Three-point terminal averaging preserved normal exposure but matched epoch-130 top-1 and worsened loss, providing no boundary-quality gain.

column5: Batch 512 with fully scaled LR curve
column6: Batch 512 gained only 6.10% image rate, projecting 141.12 passes while nearly halving decisions, so it failed the fixed gate before scoring.

column5: Continuous 65%-anchored hard-tail cosine rephase
column6: Increasing hard-tail LR area 39.46% preserved exposure but lost 0.50 points and worsened loss; retain the accepted global cosine.

column6: Two-transition average-pooled shortcuts retained 129.10 passes but lost 0.37 points, so single-phase bypasses were not limiting.
